environment: github:eswrops/EventForge (live API inspection via gh CLI, account eswrops)

checks.description: Actual GitHub OIDC subject format for environment jobs
checks.detail: Repo policies and scripts/ci/configure-oci-wif.sh require sub == 'repo:<owner>/<repo>:environment:<env>' (GitHub environment jobs) and validate iss, aud, repository, environment, and exp before exchange. The live JWT itself could not be fetched from this workstation (id-token is only issued to Actions jobs), so the claim assertions are verified by the committed checker plus fixture tests, not by a live token capture.

GET /repos/eswrops/EventForge/environments returned total_count: 0. The environment does not exist, so it carries no required reviewers and no deployment branch policy. Because jobs reference 'environment: production-plan', the first dispatch would have GitHub auto-create it with NO protection rules.
GET /branches/main/protection returned 404 'Branch not protected'. Any collaborator can push to main, and the plan/apply/preflight/backend workflows self-gate only on github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'.

checks.description: Required reviewer availability for the account plan
checks.detail: The repository is public; GitHub provides environment deployment protection rules, including required reviewers and deployment branch policies, on public repositories for all plans. The single collaborator (eswrops, admin) can serve as the required reviewer.

checks.description: Separate plan/apply OAuth clients and separate OCI trust policies
checks.detail: No OCI_WIF_CONFIG_JSON secret exists at repository or environment level (Actions secrets list is empty), so no trust boundaries exist yet. The repository design (docs/bootstrap.md, infra/bootstrap/variables.tf) mandates separate production-plan and production JSON secrets, separate OAuth clients, and separate policy statements; the OCI side has no dynamic groups and no GitHub/WIF policies (verified live), so neither trust exists yet.

default_workflow_permissions = 'read'; can_approve_pull_request_reviews = false. Each workflow also declares least-privilege permissions blocks (contents: read; id-token: write only where federation is used; contents: write only for releases).

production-plan uses group 'eventforge-production-plan', production uses 'eventforge-production-apply', backend validation 'eventforge-oci-backend-validation', frontend 'eventforge-production-frontend'; all with cancel-in-progress: false so a plan cannot be cancelled mid-run by a newer dispatch.

checks.description: Allowed Actions and SHA pinning enforcement
checks.detail: allowed_actions = 'all' and sha_pinning_required = false. The committed workflows are all SHA-pinned, but the repository does not enforce it. Hardening recommendation: restrict allowed actions to the selected set and enable SHA pinning enforcement. No protection was weakened during this acceptance.
The REST endpoint for fork workflow approval settings is not exposed for user-owned repositories (404); verify in Settings > Actions via the web UI and record in the operator evidence log.
secret_scanning enabled, secret_scanning_push_protection enabled. (validity checks and non-provider patterns are disabled — optional hardening.)

notes: An environment name alone does not create an approval boundary; production-plan/production must be created with required reviewers and a deployment branch policy restricted to main before any live federation test is run from them.
